title: Speaking Part 1 — one question, one card
note: Chapters of five questions; each question has three answers at B2 — Default, Alternative 1, Alternative 2 — that differ in angle and shape, not level. Plain teenage English: short sentences, no idioms, the expansion kept. Each answer is stored once in speaking order, with a 'frame': the answer reduced to its reusable skeleton. Answers land at 13–19 s (2.5 words/s); the builder checks.
tip: Don't memorise answers. Memorise frames — then fill them with your own life.

x.name: React
x.hint: how the question makes you feel, before you answer it
x.ask: Now put a reaction in front — how does the question make you feel?

a.name: Answer
a.hint: say it straight, in one go

r.name: Reason
r.hint: why — the part the examiner could never guess

e.name: Example
e.hint: one real moment: a day, a place, a person
e.ask: Now prove it with one real moment.

c.name: Contrast
c.hint: the 'but' — the other side that makes it sound real

cards.question: Where are you from?

alts.frame: I'm from ___, and I've lived here all my life. I really like it, mainly because ___. In the evenings, ___.
alts.why: A simple question, a simple shape: say it, say why, then one picture of your life there.

segs.t: I'm from Funchal, and I've lived here all my life.
I really like it, mainly because it's safe and the weather is good almost all year.

wrong.t: I'm from Funchal, which is the capital of Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Funchal is a city with approximately 100,000 inhabitants.
wrong.why: A fact from Wikipedia, not a reason. The examiner wants why YOU like it.

segs.t: In the evenings, my friends and I often walk along the seafront and watch the cruise ships.

wrong.t: For example, Funchal has lots of nice places.
wrong.why: Vague. One place, one habit, one picture.

wrong.t: Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
wrong.why: A statistic in disguise. What do YOU do?

alts.frame: Well, it's a bit complicated. I was born in ___, but ___ when I was ___. So now I say I'm from ___, but when ___, I feel ___ again!
alts.why: A 'complicated' answer is a gift in Part 1: the 'but' at the end shows you can hold two ideas at once.

segs.t: Well, it's a bit complicated.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

wrong.t: I am from Venezuela and Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer, and it skips the reaction. Show the question made you think first.

segs.t: I was born in Venezuela, but my family moved back to Madeira when I was five.
So now I say I'm from Funchal, but when my grandma makes arepas, I feel Venezuelan again!

wrong.t: So I'm from Funchal and I like it very much.
wrong.why: No turn. The 'but' should swing back to the other side of you.

wrong.t: However, many Madeirans emigrated to Venezuela in the past.
wrong.why: History lesson. The contrast should be about you, not the island.

alts.frame: I'm from ___, a small ___ near ___. It's the kind of place where ___. Last week ___, and ___!
alts.why: No reaction, straight in. Then one tiny story proves the 'everyone knows you' idea instead of just saying it.

segs.t: I'm from Câmara de Lobos, a small fishing town near Funchal.
It's the kind of place where everyone knows you. Last week I forgot my wallet at the bakery, and the owner gave it to my mum!
marks: It's the kind of place where

wrong.t: For example, it has many restaurants and shops.
wrong.why: A list, not a moment. What happened, to you, once?

wrong.t: It is famous because Winston Churchill painted there.
wrong.why: True, and interesting — but it's a guidebook fact, not your example.

cards.question: What's your home like?

alts.frame: We live in a ___ on the ___ floor in ___. From the balcony, we can ___. The only problem is that ___. I have to ___!
alts.why: Describe it, then complain a little. A small 'but' makes a description sound like a real opinion.

segs.t: We live in a flat on the fourth floor in São Martinho. From the balcony, we can see the sea.
The only problem is that it's quite small. I have to share a room with my little brother!

wrong.t: Also, it has two bathrooms and a kitchen.
wrong.why: 'Also' adds another fact. A contrast turns the other way.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, the apartment presents certain disadvantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Well, it's quite an ___ house. We live with ___ in ___, and there's ___. It's ___ in winter, but I prefer it to ___.
alts.why: The reaction warns the examiner there's a story. 'I prefer it to a modern flat' shows affection without saying 'I love it'.

segs.t: Well, it's quite an old house.

wrong.t: My house is an old house.
wrong.why: Flat and repetitive. React with a feeling, not a label.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: We live with my grandparents in Santo António, and there's a big garden with banana trees and chickens.
It's very cold in winter, but I prefer it to a modern flat.

wrong.t: It's freezing in winter, and it's also very old.
wrong.why: Two complaints in a row. The 'but' needs to swing back to what you love.

wrong.t: In contrast, modern flats have central heating.
wrong.why: About flats in general, not about your home.

alts.frame: It's a normal ___, nothing special, but I love ___. It's the only place where I can ___. Last month ___, and ___!
alts.why: 'Nothing special, but…' is a lovely move: lower expectations, then surprise. The example makes it funny.

segs.t: It's a normal house, nothing special, but I love my bedroom.
It's the only place where I can close the door, listen to music and relax.

wrong.t: My bedroom is my favourite room in the house.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Bedrooms are important for teenagers' mental health.
wrong.why: A magazine headline. Say why it matters to you.

segs.t: Last month I painted one wall dark blue, and my mum was not happy at all!

wrong.t: For example, I have a bed and a desk.
wrong.why: An inventory, not a moment.

wrong.t: I like the colour blue very much.
wrong.why: A preference, not an example. What happened?

cards.question: Who are you most like in your family?

alts.frame: I'm most like my ___. We both ___, and we can ___ for hours. Last summer we ___. The big difference is that she's ___, and I'm not!
alts.why: Answer, one shared moment, then the difference. The joke at the end is the contrast.

segs.t: I'm most like my mum. We both love being outside, and we can talk for hours.
Last summer we did a levada walk together and talked all the way.

wrong.t: For example, we are both very similar.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Levadas are irrigation channels built centuries ago.
wrong.why: A guidebook fact. The example is what you two did.

segs.t: The big difference is that she's very patient, and I'm not!

wrong.t: And she's also really kind and friendly.
wrong.why: More similarities. The contrast has to show a difference.

wrong.t: However, personality is influenced by many factors.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Everyone says I'm like my ___. We have the same ___, we ___, and we both ___. Sometimes it's a bit annoying, but to be honest, I'm happy to be like ___.
alts.why: A slightly annoyed start, then a soft ending that changes direction. That change of heart sounds real.

segs.t: Everyone says I'm like my dad.

wrong.t: I am most similar to my father.
wrong.why: That's the answer, stated stiffly. The reaction is how you feel about it.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: We have the same laugh, we tell the same terrible jokes, and we both support Marítimo.
Sometimes it's a bit annoying, but to be honest, I'm happy to be like him.

wrong.t: And he also loves football.
wrong.why: That's another similarity. The 'but' should turn the answer.

wrong.t: On the other hand, my mother is also nice.
wrong.why: Changes the subject instead of turning the feeling.

alts.frame: Well, probably my ___. She ___ when I was little, and she taught me to ___. We're both quite ___, but ___.
alts.why: A hesitation, a surprising answer, a detail with a comparison in it. The reason is about character, not appearance.

segs.t: Well, probably my grandma.

wrong.t: Definitely, one hundred per cent, my grandma!
wrong.why: Too certain for a surprising answer. 'Well, probably…' sounds like you're thinking.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: She moved in with us when I was little, and she taught me to cook.
We're both quite quiet, but we notice everything. My family calls us 'the detectives'.

wrong.t: She taught me to cook when I was young.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Grandparents play an important role in Portuguese families.
wrong.why: A sociology point. Why are YOU like her?

cards.question: Do you go on holiday with your family?

alts.frame: Yes, but we usually ___. Last summer we ___. We don't ___ very often, because ___.
alts.why: Answer, one real holiday, then the honest 'but'. Simple and complete.

segs.t: Yes, but we usually stay on the island.
Last summer we spent a week in Porto Moniz and swam in the natural pools every day.

wrong.t: For example, we go on holiday in Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Porto Moniz is in the north-west of the island.
wrong.why: Geography, not a memory.

segs.t: We don't travel abroad very often, because flights from Madeira are very expensive.

wrong.t: We also go to the beach a lot.
wrong.why: Adds, doesn't turn.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, domestic tourism has several advantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Not as often as I'd like! My parents ___, so ___. So we usually ___. It sounds strange, but ___!
alts.why: 'Not as often as I'd like' is a reaction and an answer in one. 'It sounds strange, but…' turns a complaint into something good.

segs.t: Not as often as I'd like!

wrong.t: No.
wrong.why: A closed door. React with the feeling behind it.

wrong.t: Holidays are important for families.
wrong.why: A general statement, not a reaction.

segs.t: My parents both work in hotels, so summer is their busiest time.
So we usually go away in November. It sounds strange, but the beaches in Porto Santo are empty!

wrong.t: So we don't go on holiday in summer.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: However, the hotel industry is essential to Madeira's economy.
wrong.why: True, but now you're writing an essay about tourism.

alts.frame: Yes, every ___ we ___. It's the only time ___, so it's ___ but ___. Last year ___, and we had to ___!
alts.why: Reason plus a funny example. The example does the proving: you don't need to say 'it's noisy', you show it.

segs.t: Yes, every August we fly to Lisbon to visit my cousins.
It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's noisy but amazing.

wrong.t: We go to Lisbon because my cousins live in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Circular — it repeats the answer.

wrong.t: Lisbon is a beautiful and historic city.
wrong.why: About Lisbon, not about why the trip matters.

segs.t: Last year fourteen of us stayed in one flat, and we had to take turns in the shower!

wrong.t: For example, we visit lots of places in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Vague. One moment you could film.

wrong.t: My cousins are the same age as me.
wrong.why: A fact, not a moment.

cards.question: Who do you spend time with at the weekend?

alts.frame: Mostly my ___. It's a very ___ thing! Every Sunday we ___. It can be a bit ___, but I would really miss it if ___.
alts.why: A reaction with a smile, a fact, then a mixed feeling. 'I would miss it if we stopped' is a second conditional doing emotional work.

segs.t: Mostly my family. It's a very Madeiran thing!

wrong.t: I spend time with my family at weekends.
wrong.why: That's the answer, not a reaction. How does the question make you feel?

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every Sunday we have a big lunch at my grandparents' house in Câmara de Lobos.
It can be a bit boring, but I would really miss it if we stopped.
marks: I would really miss it if

wrong.t: It's also really delicious and fun.
wrong.why: No turn. Where's the other side?

wrong.t: However, some teenagers prefer to spend time with friends.
wrong.why: About 'some teenagers', not you.

alts.frame: My ___, definitely. On ___ we ___. It sounds a bit silly, but it's the only time we can ___. Last ___ we ___!
alts.why: 'It sounds a bit silly, but…' defends your answer before the examiner can judge it. The example is the punchline.

segs.t: My friends, definitely. On Saturdays we meet at Forum Madeira and walk around for hours.
It sounds a bit silly, but it's the only time we can talk without our parents listening.
marks: It sounds a bit silly, but

wrong.t: We go to Forum Madeira because it's a shopping centre.
wrong.why: Obvious. Why do you go?

wrong.t: Shopping centres are popular places for young people.
wrong.why: A general fact, not your reason.

segs.t: Last Saturday we spent three hours there and didn't buy anything!

wrong.t: For example, there are many shops there.
wrong.why: About the place, not about a Saturday.

wrong.t: We like shopping very much.
wrong.why: A feeling, not a moment.

alts.frame: It depends on the ___. Every other ___ I ___, because ___. At first it felt ___, but now I ___!
alts.why: 'At first… but now' tells a change in one breath. Serious content, light ending: complex without being heavy.

segs.t: It depends on the weekend.

wrong.t: I spend time with different people.
wrong.why: Vague, and it isn't a reaction. 'It depends' buys time naturally.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every other Saturday I stay with my dad in Machico, because my parents are separated.
At first it felt strange, but now I like having two homes. Double the birthday presents!

wrong.t: It is strange to have two homes.
wrong.why: Stops at the hard part. The 'but now' is what shows how you feel today.

wrong.t: Divorce is increasingly common in modern society.
wrong.why: An essay sentence. Keep it about you.

cards.question: What's your city like?

alts.frame: It's quite ___, but there's always something to do. ___ is located between ___, so you get ___ from almost anywhere. The only downside is that ___, so it's hard to ___.
alts.why: A quick opinion, a picture, then the downside. Three moves, three different jobs.

segs.t: It's quite small, but there's always something to do.
marks: but there's always something to do

wrong.t: My city is a city in Madeira.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Funchal is located between the mountains and the sea, so you get amazing views from almost anywhere.
The only downside is that the centre gets packed with tourists in summer, so it's hard to get around.

wrong.t: Also, there are many beautiful gardens.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, tourism has both advantages and disadvantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: It's quite ___, because I live in ___, not ___. It's right next to ___, but after a while you ___. When ___, half the town ___!
alts.why: No reaction, straight in. The reason explains the noise; the example turns a problem into a local show.

segs.t: It's quite quiet, because I live in Machico, not Funchal.
It's right next to the airport, but after a while you stop noticing the planes.

wrong.t: Machico is a quiet town in the east.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Airports are important for islands.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: When it's windy and the planes can't land, half the town goes out to watch!

wrong.t: For example, many planes land there.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Madeira airport has a famous runway.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Oh, I love it, so I can't be objective! ___ feels like ___ and ___ at the same time. For example, ___, and the next morning ___!
alts.why: One clever idea — city and village at once — proved by one tiny scene.

segs.t: Oh, I love it, so I can't be objective!

wrong.t: I think it's nice.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Funchal feels like a big city and a village at the same time.
For example, you go to a concert at night, and the next morning the baker asks about it!

wrong.t: For example, there are many shops and cafés.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Funchal has about 100,000 people.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

cards.question: Where's the best place to go with friends in your city?

alts.frame: Definitely the ___. It's a ___. It's cheap, it's close to ___, and there's always ___. Last summer we ___, and we stayed until ___.
alts.why: Answer, three quick reasons in one breath, then a memory that proves it.

segs.t: Definitely the Lido. It's a big outdoor pool right next to the sea.
It's cheap, it's close to the centre, and there's always someone from school there.

wrong.t: The Lido is a swimming pool in Funchal.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Swimming is good exercise for teenagers.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Last summer we went almost every day, and we stayed until they closed the gates.

wrong.t: For example, we go there a lot.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: The Lido was renovated a few years ago.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Anywhere with ___! No, seriously, we usually go to ___. It isn't very exciting, but ___, and ___.
alts.why: A joke first, then 'No, seriously': the move that turns a joke into a real answer.

segs.t: Anywhere with free Wi-Fi!

wrong.t: The best place is a shopping centre.
wrong.why: That's the answer, and it skips the fun. React first.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: No, seriously, we usually go to the food court at Forum Madeira.
It isn't very exciting, but it's warm when it rains, the chips are cheap, and nobody asks us to leave.

wrong.t: It's also very big and modern.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, shopping centres are bad for local shops.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: The ___, especially ___. We ___ and talk for hours. Last ___ we ___ and invented funny stories about ___.
alts.why: No reaction, no reason: the place and one evening there. Sometimes two moves are enough.

segs.t: The seafront, especially at sunset. We sit on the wall by the marina and talk for hours.
Last Friday we watched a huge cruise ship leave and invented funny stories about the passengers on board.

wrong.t: For example, the seafront is very beautiful.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

cards.question: Is there anything you'd change about your city?

alts.frame: Yes, I would definitely improve ___. They're often ___, and ___ so ___ that ___. Last week I ___ and missed ___.
alts.why: Answer, reason, and a small disaster as proof. The second conditional ('I would') is doing the work.

segs.t: Yes, I would definitely improve the buses.
They're often late, and some hills are so steep that it's difficult to walk.

wrong.t: The buses need to be better.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Public transport is essential in modern cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Last week I waited forty minutes in São Martinho and missed the start of my Maths test.

wrong.t: For example, buses are sometimes late.
wrong.why: That's the reason again. One day, one bus, one consequence.

wrong.t: The buses in Funchal are yellow.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Well, just one thing. I would make more ___, like ___. At the moment there's a lot for ___, but there isn't much for ___.
alts.why: 'At the moment… but…': the contrast is between two groups of people, and you're in one of them.

segs.t: Well, just one thing.

wrong.t: Yes, I would change many things.
wrong.why: Not a reaction, and it promises a list you won't give.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I would make more places for teenagers, like a skate park or a youth club.
At the moment there's a lot for tourists, but there isn't much for teenagers to do in the evenings.

wrong.t: Also, I'd like more cinemas.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, the city offers many facilities.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: To be honest, not much. I would just ___. It's the prettiest part of ___, with ___. But with ___, it's hard to enjoy it.
alts.why: 'Not much' — then one precise change. A small, specific answer sounds more confident than a long list.

segs.t: To be honest, not much.

wrong.t: My city is perfect.
wrong.why: Closes the door. 'Not much' leaves room for one idea.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I would just close the old town to cars at weekends.
It's the prettiest part of Funchal, with painted doors and little cafés. But with so much traffic, it's hard to enjoy it.

wrong.t: I'd ban cars because I don't like cars.
wrong.why: Circular. Why the old town?

wrong.t: Cars cause pollution in many cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: Do you travel far every day?

alts.frame: Not really. I'm lucky! I take ___, and it only takes about ___. But in the morning ___, so I usually have to ___.
alts.why: 'I'm lucky' is a reaction with a smile. 'But in the morning…' turns it around neatly.

segs.t: Not really. I'm lucky!

wrong.t: No, I don't travel far.
wrong.why: The answer, not a reaction. How do you feel about it?

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I take the bus to my school in the centre, and it only takes about twenty-five minutes.
But in the morning the bus is very full, so I usually have to stand all the way.

wrong.t: Although the bus is quite comfortable.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, traffic is a problem in many cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: Yes, quite far. I live in ___, but ___. The ___ takes about ___, but I don't mind, because ___. Last week I ___ and ___!
alts.why: A long journey needs a reason, and the example makes it funny instead of a complaint.

segs.t: Yes, quite far. I live in Camacha, but my school is in Funchal.
The bus takes about forty minutes, but I don't mind, because my school has a great music programme.

wrong.t: It's far because Camacha is far from Funchal.
wrong.why: Circular — the geography isn't a reason.

wrong.t: Many students travel long distances to school.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Last week I fell asleep on the bus and missed my stop!

wrong.t: For example, the bus takes fifty minutes.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Camacha is famous for wicker baskets.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: No, I'm really lucky. I just walk, because ___ is only ___ from ___. The only problem is that ___. Every morning I ___!
alts.why: Short journey, short answer, and a funny picture at the end so it doesn't die.

segs.t: No, I'm really lucky.

wrong.t: No.
wrong.why: A closed door. Show a feeling.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I just walk, because my school is only ten minutes from my flat.
The only problem is that it's all uphill. Every morning I arrive at school like I've just run a marathon!
marks: like I've just run a marathon

wrong.t: And the walk is really nice.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, walking is healthier than driving.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: Do you prefer going by car or by public transport?

alts.frame: I definitely prefer ___. The ___ is ___ and ___, and I can ___ on the way. The only downside is that ___, especially when ___.
alts.why: Your B2 answer, cleaned up: answer, two reasons joined naturally, and an honest downside.

segs.t: I definitely prefer public transport.
The bus is cheaper and better for the environment, and I can talk to my friends on the way.

wrong.t: I prefer the bus to the car.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Public transport reduces carbon emissions significantly.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

segs.t: The only downside is that it's sometimes late, especially when it's windy along the coast.

wrong.t: Also, the bus drivers are friendly.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, cars are more popular in Madeira.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: The ___, definitely. My ___ drives me to ___. With ___, the bus would be ___, and it takes twice as long.
alts.why: A firm reaction, then a reason that's pure logistics. 'Would be very difficult': the conditional does the imagining.

segs.t: The car, definitely.

wrong.t: I think maybe the car.
wrong.why: Too weak for how sure the rest of the answer is.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: My dad drives me to football training twice a week, and to matches at the weekend.
With my sports bag and my boots, the bus would be very difficult, and it takes twice as long.

wrong.t: I prefer the car because I like cars.

cards.question: Do you enjoy long journeys?

alts.frame: Yes, I quite enjoy ___. I just ___ and ___, because ___. But ___, so sometimes I feel a bit sick.
alts.why: Yes, why, and an honest downside.

segs.t: Yes, I quite enjoy long journeys around the island.
I just listen to music and look out of the window, because the views are amazing.

wrong.t: I enjoy them because they're long.
wrong.why: Circular.

wrong.t: Madeira is famous for its landscapes.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: But the mountain roads have lots of curves, so sometimes I feel a bit sick.

wrong.t: And the views are beautiful.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, cars cause pollution.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: Not at all! I get ___ very quickly, especially on ___. When we ___, I asked ___ twenty times. My ___ pretended to sleep!
alts.why: A strong 'no', and a funny example that everyone recognises.

segs.t: Not at all!

wrong.t: No, I don't enjoy long journeys.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I get bored very quickly, especially on planes and long bus trips.
When we flew to London last year, I asked 'Are we there yet?' twenty times. My dad pretended to sleep!

wrong.t: For example, planes are boring.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: The flight to London takes about four hours.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: It depends who I'm with. With ___, it's fine, because ___. But on ___, I often ___, and the trip feels very long.
alts.why: 'It depends who I'm with', then both sides, each with a reason.

segs.t: It depends who I'm with.

wrong.t: Sometimes.
wrong.why: Too short to be a reaction.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: With my family, it's fine, because we play silly games all the way.
But on school trips, I often sit next to someone I don't know, and the trip feels very long.

wrong.t: And my family is funny.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, travelling with friends is better.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: What's the most interesting place you've travelled to?

alts.frame: Probably ___, on ___. I went there last ___ with ___, and we ___. The ___ was ___, but ___ was unforgettable.
alts.why: Place, memory, and 'freezing, but unforgettable'.

segs.t: Probably Porto Moniz, on the north coast of the island.
I went there last summer with my family, and we swam in the natural volcanic pools.

wrong.t: For example, it is a nice place.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Porto Moniz is in the north-west of Madeira.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

segs.t: The water was freezing, but swimming next to those huge cliffs was unforgettable.

wrong.t: And the pools were very big.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, natural pools can be dangerous.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: Oh, that's easy. ___! We went ___ to visit ___, who lives there. I had never seen so many ___, and I ___!
alts.why: 'I had never seen so many…': past perfect for a first impression. Then a moment of drama.

segs.t: Oh, that's easy. London!

wrong.t: The most interesting place is London.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: We went last Christmas to visit my uncle, who lives there with his family.
I had never seen so many people in one place, and I got lost in the Underground for five minutes!
marks: I had never seen so many

wrong.t: For example, London is a big city.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: London has about nine million people.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: The ___, near ___. Nobody lives there, because ___, so you can only visit ___. We saw ___ on the way, and I was so excited that I nearly ___!
alts.why: A surprising, local answer — explained, then brought to life.

segs.t: The Desertas Islands, near Madeira.
Nobody lives there, because it's a nature reserve, so you can only visit on special boat trips.

wrong.t: They are islands near Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Nature reserves protect endangered species.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: We saw dolphins on the way, and I was so excited that I nearly fell off the boat!

wrong.t: For example, there are many animals.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Monk seals live on the Desertas.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

cards.question: Which country would you most like to visit?

alts.frame: Oh, ___, definitely! I'm a huge ___ fan, so I'd love to ___. It's quite expensive to ___, but I'm determined to go one day.
alts.why: Country, reason, and 'but I'm determined'.

segs.t: Oh, England, definitely!

wrong.t: I would like to visit England.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I'm a huge Harry Potter fan, so I'd love to visit the film studios in London.
It's quite expensive to travel from Madeira, but I'm determined to go one day.

wrong.t: And London is a big city.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, England has bad weather.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: ___, I think, or maybe ___. I love ___, and ___ look completely different from ___. My parents think ___, but I've already started ___.
alts.why: No reaction, straight in. The contrast shows determination with a present perfect.

segs.t: Japan, I think, or maybe South Korea.
I love anime, and the food and the cities look completely different from Madeira.

wrong.t: I'd like to go because it's Japan.
wrong.why: Circular.

wrong.t: Japan is a popular tourist destination.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: My parents think it's too far, but I've already started saving my birthday money.

wrong.t: And Japan has many temples.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, flights to Japan are expensive.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: ___, actually. My ___ was born there, and she always ___. I'd love to see ___, and meet ___.
alts.why: A family reason: the Madeira–Venezuela link is real for many students. 'The cousins I only know from video calls' is a lovely detail.

segs.t: Venezuela, actually.

wrong.t: Venezuela.
wrong.why: Just the answer.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: My grandma was born there, and she always tells me stories about it at dinner.
I'd love to see the places she talks about, and meet the cousins I only know from video calls.

wrong.t: I want to go because my grandma is from there.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Many Madeirans emigrated to Venezuela.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: What do you like doing on holiday?

alts.frame: I love ___, especially ___. ___ is so relaxing, and ___. The only problem is that ___, so we have to ___.
alts.why: What, why, and the only problem.

segs.t: I love going to the beach, especially the natural pools in Porto Moniz or Seixal.
Swimming there is so relaxing, and the water is really clear.

wrong.t: I like the beach because it's the beach.
wrong.why: Circular.

wrong.t: Beaches are popular in summer.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: The only problem is that they get really crowded in summer, so we have to arrive early.

wrong.t: And the sand is very black.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, sunbathing can be dangerous.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: To be honest, nothing at all! I just want to ___. But after about a week, I usually ___ and start ___.
alts.why: An honest reaction, then a twist about yourself. 'Start annoying my little brother' is funny and real.

segs.t: To be honest, nothing at all!

wrong.t: I like relaxing on holiday.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I just want to sleep late, play games with my friends and forget about school.
But after about a week, I usually get bored and start annoying my little brother.

wrong.t: And I also watch TV.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, holidays are important for rest.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: I love ___, especially ___. Last ___ we ___. The ___ were incredible. My ___ complained all the way, though!
alts.why: Answer, one walk, and a funny 'though' about someone else.

segs.t: I love exploring new places, especially on foot.
Last holiday we walked the São Lourenço trail, at the eastern end of the island. The colours of the cliffs were incredible.

wrong.t: For example, I like walking.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Ponta de São Lourenço is a nature reserve.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

segs.t: My brother complained all the way, though!

wrong.t: And it was very sunny.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, walking can be tiring.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: Do you enjoy travelling?

alts.frame: I love it, but only when I get there! Every ___ we ___, and ___. The ___, on the other hand, is ___. It's ___ of ___!
alts.why: The reaction already hints at a 'but', and the contrast pays it off.

segs.t: I love it, but only when I get there!
marks: but only when I get there

wrong.t: Yes, I enjoy travelling.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: Travelling is something that many people enjoy.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

segs.t: Every summer we take the ferry to Porto Santo, and the beach there is nine kilometres long.
The ferry, on the other hand, is horrible. It's two and a half hours of feeling sick!

wrong.t: On the other hand, Porto Santo is also beautiful.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, travelling can be expensive.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: Not really, and it's because of ___. ___ is famous for ___, so ___ all the time. Last ___ we were stuck in ___, and ___.
alts.why: A surprising 'no' needs a reason fast, and the reason needs proof.

segs.t: Not really, and it's because of the airport.
Our airport is famous for strong winds, so flights are cancelled all the time.

wrong.t: I don't like travelling because I don't enjoy it.
wrong.why: Circular.

wrong.t: Airports are big buildings.
wrong.why: A description, not a reason.

segs.t: Last Christmas we were stuck in Lisbon for two days, and my little sister cried the whole time.

wrong.t: For example, many flights are cancelled.
wrong.why: That's the reason again.

wrong.t: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: I'd love to travel more, to be honest. I've only ___ twice, both times to ___. ___ is really expensive, and ___ at the same time.
alts.why: A wish, the facts, and an honest reason why not.

segs.t: I'd love to travel more, to be honest.

wrong.t: Travel is very important in the modern world.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I've only left the island twice, both times to visit my cousins in Jersey.
Flying from Madeira is really expensive, and my parents rarely have holidays at the same time.

wrong.t: I've been to Jersey twice.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Travelling helps you learn about other cultures.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.
